title: Binomial Squares

misconceptions.label: Forgot the 2ab middle term
misconceptions.claim: I think (x+3)^2 is just x^2 + 9, because you square each part and there is no middle term.
probes: What do you get when you write (x+3)(x+3) before simplifying?
In (a+b)^2, why is there a 2ab term?

misconceptions.label: Distribution or sign slip
misconceptions.claim: I think (x+3)^2 is x^2 + 3x + 9, because x times x is x^2, x times 3 is 3x, and 3 times 3 is 9, and that's all.
probes: Can you multiply x+3 by x, then by 3, and add the results?
What sign does each partial product carry?

misconceptions.label: Applied (a+b)^n = a^n + b^n
misconceptions.claim: I believe the square just goes onto each term, so (a+b)^2 always equals a^2 + b^2.
probes: Does the power apply to every term inside the bracket separately?

en: Start with a square of side x plus 3.
The big square has area x squared.
Each rectangle has area three x.
Together the two rectangles make six x.
The small square has area nine.
So x plus three all squared equals x squared plus six x plus nine.
ur: ایک مربع لیں جس کی طرف x plus 3 ہو۔
بڑے مربع کا رقبہ x squared ہے۔
دونوں مستطیلوں کا مجموعہ 6x بنتا ہے۔

notes: Binomial square pack for the Judge Test Path. Area-model board task graded by template element IDs; algebra graded by mathjs.
